correctness.rationale: The common zero locus of two independent alternating forms on rank-two U is a two-hyperplane Plucker complete intersection in Gr(2,2n+1), of expected codimension two and smooth by the source. The individual defining forms have rank 2n, forcing their Plucker hypersurfaces smooth (a singular two-plane would be contained in their one-dimensional radicals). For \(n\ge2\) the final dimension is >=4; integral Lefschetz yields \(H^2\)=Z with restricted Plucker class primitive. Intersecting the defining hyperplanes gives top cup power deg Gr(2,2n+1)=\(C_{2n-1}\); for Gr(2,2n) it is \(C_{2n-2}\). Pieri ballot counts prove the formulas for arbitrary n; factorial algebra gives \(C_{2n-1}\)/\(C_{2n-2}\)=(4n-3)/n>1. The invariant absolute integer top-power coefficient is preserved by any graded integral ring isomorphism. Both spaces are cellular so the identical argument applies to their integral Chow rings. The extracted self-contained Python checker returned VERIFY_OK for degree/sample dimension checks; finite testing is not substituted for the uniform proof.

value.rationale: The explicit motivating gap is Remark 1.2 of arXiv:2610.03309v1: surprising equality of additive cohomology does not determine multiplication. The theorem determines a natural primitive hyperplane top-product for every member of the entire rank-two biisotropic family, and gives a uniform sharp negative answer to the ring-isomorphism portion of that gap, over both integral cohomology and Chow rings. This is structural integral information (not a numerical slice or a mere coefficient conversion), identifies \(n=1\) as the sharp equal boundary, and shows why additive or even Chow-motivic agreement does not imply multiplicative agreement. The known Catalan and Lefschetz steps are openly identified as standard. The full presentations and other k remain open.
